newsitem.title: GREECE: Yugoslav PM calls for more trade with Greece.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav PM calls for more trade with Greece.

text.p: Visiting Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic said on Wednesday he wanted more trade with Greece and asked Athens' backing for Yugoslavia to be reintegrated into international organisations.

"We had friendly and constructive talks on promoting bilateral relations, Balkan cooperation and the reintegration of Yugoslavia in international bodies," Kontic told reporters after a meeting with Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
"But we mainly focused in promoting bilateral economic ties which are developing very well," he said.
He said Greece and Yugoslavia signed two bilateral treaties to protect investments and avoid double-taxation.

Greek banks were soon expected to issue credits to Belgrade for purchasing Greek goods and Kordic said Simitis had agreed in principle for Yugoslav businesses to ship their goods from the northern Greek port of Salonika.
Simitis said Greek interest for investing in Yugoslavia was high and would continue to grow.

He cited recent investments involving the $392 million acquisition of 20 percent of the Serbian Telecom Srbija by the Greek telecom OTE and a $517 deal between Greek metals trading firm Mytilineos and RMHK Trepca mines.
The deal involves the modernisation of the Yugoslav mines and the distibution of the final product to international markets.
Kontic also urged liberalisation in movement of people, capital and goods between the two countries with a final aim of setting up a free trade zone in the Balkans.
He said Greece had agreed to back Yugoslavia in its effort to be reintegrated in international bodies like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Greece is a traditional ally of Belgrade and backed the Serbian government throughout the war in former Yugoslavia.
